Two paths

What you can ask for.

Video for social media and YouTube

Voice-over, music, effects and on-screen text. Two lines: short vertical up to 60 seconds, in the network's format, and long-form narrated, faceless, 10 to 20 minutes, ready for YouTube.

  • Script from your brief, or editing from the script you bring
  • One revision round on the pilot, two after that
  • First cut in 3 calendar days for short, 5 for long-form, from the brief

Scope, deadline and price agreed in writing.

Automation and agents with evidence

Routines, integrations and agents that work on their own — and leave a receipt of what they did. The contract is public; scope and price come in the proposal.

  • Every run records what ran, when, and what came back
  • Runs on your server or on Edge Build Labs' own
  • Delivered with the evidence contract applied

Scope, deadline and price agreed in writing.

Living World

A public Ultima Online shard (T2A era, on ModernUO), running since 5 September 2026 on a single VPS. Rootless container, image pinned by digest, daily backup with a restore that was actually performed.

livingworld.edgebuildlabs.tech→

evidence-contracts

Three public-domain files (CC0), no dependencies, no install. Copy one into your repository: it is the instruction set that makes your agent report what it ran, when, and what came back.

github.com/edgebuildlabs/evidence-contracts→

work-order-contract

How to ask for the work so that proof is possible: goal, state, scope, acceptance, limits, evidence and stop. A public-domain template (CC0).

github.com/edgebuildlabs/work-order-contract→

channel-contract

How you talk to an agent running on a machine you do not control, and how its delivery outlives the session: a repository used as a channel, with the contract inside it. Extracted from a channel that ran for six days with five agents. Public domain (CC0).

github.com/edgebuildlabs/channel-contract→

How the work is checked

The ladder.

Four words an agent confuses. Not here.

  1. STARTED

    The process began. That is all.

  2. ≠COMPLETED

    The agent says it is done. That is a sentence, not a fact.

  3. ≠VALIDATED

    Someone read the result off the machine: the file, the log, the test.

  4. ≠PASS

    What was asked matches what was delivered, with a source and a date.

Every claim of state carries a source and a date, or the words NOT VERIFIED.

Running agents on real infrastructure? The whole method is on the thesis site.
